So I got my first stripped lower!

Buy all the things.

Primary Arms is a good place to start. Compare prices between them, MidwayUSA & JoeBobOutfitters. If you have a Cabella's or Gander Mountain (or other sporting goods store near you), check for sales on BUIS, slings, optics and mags.

Do you have a lower parts kit yet?

Expect to dump ~$1,300 after all is said and done. You could get away with less, depending on what you're looking for, and depending on how much you buy on sale. Compare prices on everything.

Lower parts kit. Super cheap.

Tools to put it together, can be costly.

Define what it is you want from your rifle. Then look for the other pieces to accomplish it. Upper, bolt carrier group, charging handle, barrell length, rail, gas system, etc.
Do the lower parts kits have any variance other than brand and quality? I am wanting to build a carbine variant. Does that matter at all in picking the lower parts kit?

As long as we're talking about only the lower receiver---no, it should not.

Lower parts kit will include:

  • Pistol grip & mounting hardware
  • Various detents for safety, buffer tube & takedown pins
  • Springs for those detents
  • Trigger assembly (which you may end up replacing later on (it depends on how light and crisp you need/want it))
  • Safety selector
  • Trigger guard
  • Mag release button & hardware
  • Bolt catch
  • Roll pins for securing bolt catch & trigger guard

None of those things should affect a carbine build in any way. Same really should go for stock & upper receiver as well. The only difference should be the barrel & gas tube. It should be safe to build everything else as normal. That's the beauty of the AR-15 platform.

I've heard good things about DPMS parts kits, but I think as long as you're buying from a firearms shop (not ebay or amazon), and reading reviews, you should be safe. I would just get mil-spec and go on to the next thing.

FYI Bravo company is selling blemished uppers for $80.00 right now. I would go ahead and buy a BCG from them while you're at it.

I used a CMMG parts kit and it works great. (I swapped out the plastic grip for a Hogue, personally)
